# Agent movement corpora: coverage analysis

<!-- Generated by tools/corpus_analysis.py; do not edit by hand. -->

**Data as of:** 2026-10-16 (latest `date_accessed` in the input records) · **Items:** 100 news ([source](../news-corpus/news.jsonl)), 83 papers ([source](../paper-corpus/papers.jsonl))

> **Scope of these numbers.** Every table below is a descriptive count of the two curated corpora. The counts are shaped by the sampling protocol: a fixed set of search themes, a capped number of candidates per theme, theme-balanced selection for news, a fixed news publication window, and a single search date. They are not estimates of how activity or publication is distributed in the field, and no causal reading is intended. Percentages are shares of the corpus in question.

## 5. Crosswalk to the four movement operations

The [project README](../../README.md) defines four operations: delegation / handoff, portable task context, runtime relocation and cross-framework migration. This crosswalk counts how many items *touch* each one under a keyword rule, and sets that beside the curated `movement_operations` codes.

**Rule (heuristic).** Concatenate `title` and `summary`; an item touches an operation if any keyword below matches case-insensitively at the start of a word (regex `\b` + keyword, open-ended, so keywords act as stems). An item can touch several operations. The rule is a transparent screen, not a validated classifier: it has not been checked against human judgement, it misses paraphrases, and broad stems (for example `memory`, `interoperab`, `resum`) will over-count. Treat agreement with the coded labels as a rough consistency check only.

| Operation | Keywords |
| --- | --- |
| Delegation / handoff | `delegat`, `handoff`, `hand-off`, `hand off`, `handover`, `hand over`, `agent-to-agent`, `a2a`, `subagent`, `sub-agent`, `contract net`, `task assignment`, `task allocation`, `on behalf of` |
| Portable task context | `portable context`, `task context`, `context transfer`, `context sharing`, `shared context`, `context management`, `context engineering`, `memory`, `checkpoint`, `session state`, `agent state`, `state transfer`, `persistent state`, `serializ`, `snapshot`, `artifact reference`, `resumable` |
| Runtime relocation | `relocat`, `mobile agent`, `agent mobility`, `code mobility`, `process migration`, `live migration`, `vm migration`, `virtual machine migration`, `durable`, `idempoten`, `safe boundary`, `resum`, `suspend`, `failover`, `crash recovery`, `fault toleran` |
| Cross-framework migration | `cross-framework`, `framework-agnostic`, `framework agnostic`, `framework-independent`, `framework-neutral`, `interoperab`, `adapter`, `lock-in`, `portabil`, `agent spec`, `agent specification`, `agent definition`, `declarative agent`, `agent file`, `portable representation`, `across frameworks`, `across runtimes`, `cross-runtime`, `different runtime` |

Columns: *Keyword hits* = items matched by the rule; *Coded* = items whose `movement_operations` include the operation; *Both*, *Keyword only*, *Coded only* compare the two sets.

## 6. Coverage gaps (hypotheses for the next search round)

Rules: a cell is listed when its count is ≤ 1. For year × theme, only the last 4 years present in each corpus are checked, because older years are sparse by design. Every entry is a **hypothesis**: a low count may mean the topic is genuinely thin, or only that the search queries, the per-theme caps, the ranking tie-breaks or the single search date did not surface it. In particular, news selection ranked items newest-first within each theme before the per-theme cut, which by itself depresses counts for the earliest years of the news window. Each entry can be tested with targeted queries in the next round.

### Core operations overall

- **H36.** News: the least-coded core operation is portable task context (16 coded, 16 keyword hits, of 100). Hypothesis: it is under-represented relative to the other three operations in this corpus; a search round with queries aimed specifically at it would test whether that reflects the field or the theme definitions.
